answer: Paragraph 14 most naturally attaches “upon SFC’s request” to demonstration, leaving confirmation unconditioned by a request. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; “to the SFC’s satisfaction” expressly qualifies demonstration. Footnote 5 supplies minimum content for both confirmation and demonstration: compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and assurance, with a high level of confidence, against smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws. Its omission of the request condition supports a rival standing-demonstration reading, although that reading must confront the express condition in paragraph 14. With no request, confirmation remains applicable, while demonstration is untriggered under the main-text and integrated readings but remains applicable under the standing-footnote reading. None of this establishes fulfillment. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory supporting legal opinion on the relevant SFC request.

claims.inference: Text and grammatical deduction: the inserted request clause immediately precedes “demonstrate”; the satisfaction standard likewise follows that verb. The listed subjects are shared by confirmation and demonstration. Extending the satisfaction standard independently to confirmation requires an additional interpretation.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the Product Provider, product, activity and assessment interval, including relevant conditions or modifications.
Any authoritative interpretation resolving the scope of the satisfaction standard.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 supports confirmation without a request and request-triggered demonstration to the SFC’s satisfaction, concerning the same listed subjects.
claims.status: Source-supported interpretation; not a certified legal conclusion

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

claims.inference: Text: footnote 5 joins both verbs to the same minimum content. Grammatical judgment: “with a high level of confidence” most naturally concerns the absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws. It supplies no numerical threshold or prescribed proof method, and is not expressly synonymous with SFC satisfaction.
missing_premises: An applicable interpretation and evidential standard for “high level of confidence”.
Evidence of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and assessment of the relevant smart contracts.
claims.proposition: Footnote 5 elaborates the object of both confirmation and demonstration, with a confidence standard for smart-contract assurance.
claims.status: Express minimum content; standard partly unresolved

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

claims.inference: Conditional deduction: assuming applicability and an established absence of a relevant request, readings A and C leave demonstration untriggered; reading B does not. Confirmation remains unconditioned by a request in each reading. An absent record of a request is not itself proof that no request was made. Neither applicability nor absence of a trigger proves substantive compliance.
missing_premises: Facts establishing whether an applicable request was made and its scope.
Resolution of the main-text/footnote attachment dispute.
Actual confirmation, supporting evidence and an applicable fulfillment standard.
claims.proposition: No-request consequences depend on the retained rival reading, and do not establish fulfillment or excuse the underlying requirements.

Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above

claims.inference: Text and deduction: paragraph 15 requires obtaining external audit or verification upon the relevant request, rather than simply making the Provider’s confirmation or demonstration. The passage does not expressly repeat either paragraph 14’s satisfaction standard or footnote 5’s confidence formulation.
missing_premises: Applicability and the terms of any request for third-party audit or verification.
Evidence that the required audit or verification was obtained and met its applicable scope and standard.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 15 separately addresses request-triggered third-party audit or verification of the same three subject areas.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: paragraph 16’s object is a legal opinion supporting the application, with an express “satisfactory” qualification. A paragraph 14 demonstration request does not automatically establish a request for this opinion or for paragraph 15 audit; a single communication could request several actions if its terms do so.
missing_premises: The relevant application and any applicable SFC request.
The applicable meaning of “satisfactory” and evidence that the opinion satisfies it.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 16 separately conditions obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application on an SFC request.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: confirmation is not request-conditioned; demonstration of paragraph 14’s subjects is request-triggered and subject to SFC satisfaction. Footnote 5’s precise integration remains unresolved.

B — Standing-footnote reading: footnote 5’s unqualified “confirm and demonstrate” supports standing demonstration of its minimum content. This reading must explain why paragraph 14 expressly conditions demonstration on a request.

C — Integrated reading: footnote 5 supplies minimum content for both acts while paragraph 14 retains the request trigger and SFC-satisfaction standard for demonstration. This is the stronger textual reconciliation because it gives effect to both provisions, but is an interpretive judgment rather than an established authoritative resolution.
unresolved: The retained sources do not conclusively resolve the main-text/footnote tension or the full attachment of the satisfaction and confidence standards.
No entity-specific applicability, request history, confirmation, demonstration or fulfillment evidence is supplied.
The provisions use “should”; their precise legal effect must not be upgraded to an unconditional statutory duty from the wording or candidate encoding alone.
Parser acceptance, Boolean equivalence, graph results and serialization checks do not establish the legal validity of any reading.
